analyzed_vuln.description: SkTriangulateSimplePolygon classifies reflex vertices by calling ReflexHash::add, which computes a grid index via ReflexHash::hash and then does fGrid[index].addToTail(v) without validating index bounds. For degenerate polygons (notably zero-width/zero-height bounds from repeated/collinear points), init() can produce fVCount==0 and/or invalid grid conversion, so hash() returns a negative or out-of-range index. This causes out-of-bounds access of fGrid and then a crash in SkTInternalLList::addToTail when writing through a bogus list object.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In api_polyutils (skia/fuzz/FuzzPolyUtils.cpp), fuzz input controls point count and coordinates passed to SkTriangulateSimplePolygon. A crafted polygon with size >=3 and non-zero winding but degenerate bounds (e.g., width or height ~0) can pass early checks, then during reflex classification at SkTriangulateSimplePolygon line ~1615, reflexHash.add() is called on at least one reflex vertex. Because ReflexHash::init/hash do not enforce valid grid dimensions/index range, hash index can be invalid, leading to OOB fGrid access and SEGV in addToTail.
